# Postgres to Apache Doris

[Apache Doris](https://doris.apache.org/) is a columnar analytical database that speaks the MySQL
protocol. Since 4.1 it can follow Postgres by itself: one statement creates the target tables,
copies the rows and streams changes from a replication slot, with no Kafka or Debezium deployment
in between.

```sql
CREATE JOB pg_mirror_job
PROPERTIES ("max_interval" = "1")
ON STREAMING
FROM POSTGRES (
    "jdbc_url" = "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/app",
    "driver_url" = "https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.4/postgresql-42.7.4.jar",
    "driver_class" = "org.postgresql.Driver",
    "user" = "app", "password" = "...",
    "database" = "app", "schema" = "doris_src",
    "include_tables" = "docs",
    "offset" = "initial"
)
TO DATABASE pg_mirror ("table.create.properties.replication_num" = "1");
```

The lab runs one frontend and one backend next to pg16 and pointed a job at the project's tables.
What it found on Doris 4.1.4:

| | |
|---|---|
| source side | the job creates its own publication and slot, one per job; `DROP JOB` removes both |
| latency | seconds, not milliseconds: about 11 with the default `max_interval` of 10, about 5 with 1 |
| types | `jsonb` lands as `text`, `uuid` as `text`, `timestamptz` as `datetime(6)` in the Doris time zone |
| `vector` | auto table creation refuses it; in a pre-created table it arrives as NULL, silently |
| generated columns | copied by the snapshot, then dropped once streaming starts |
| DDL | added and dropped columns propagate, which Postgres to Postgres does not do |

## The vector problem

Doris's CDC client is Debezium's Postgres connector, and Debezium has no converter for pgvector's
`vector`. The column does not fail; it arrives as NULL. The workaround the notebook verifies is a
trigger-maintained `real[]` copy of the embedding on the source, which arrives as `ARRAY<FLOAT>`,
and Doris's own `cosine_distance` then returns the same top five as pgvector.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sized for a server

The images are large (4 GB frontend, 9 GB backend), and their defaults assume a dedicated machine:
an 8 GB heap and a backend sized to 90% of memory, which on Docker Desktop ends in
`MEM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The lab's compose file caps both (`DORIS_FE_HEAP`, `DORIS_BE_MEM`) to
fit beside the other containers.
:::
